scales.label: Molecular / sequence
scales.blurb: Change non-coding DNA and leave every protein intact. This is the layer where a limb can be removed without touching anything else the gene does, and it is the layer evolution used in snakes and sticklebacks. It is also the only layer a genome language model emits a score for.

scales.label: Gene / coding
scales.blurb: Delete or break the protein. The phenotypes here are the strongest and best documented, and most of them kill the animal for a reason that has nothing to do with limbs - lung, kidney, allantois, heart. The gene scale tells you what a node does; it rarely gives you an animal.

scales.label: Cell / signalling centre
scales.blurb: Remove or silence the AER or the ZPA as structures, rather than the genes that specify them. This is where the subject started, with a scalpel, and it is where the timing question is posed most directly: cut the ridge off later and you get more limb.

scales.label: Tissue / maintenance loop
scales.blurb: The circuit that decides how long the bud keeps growing: a SHH-GREM1-FGF loop that is self-promoting AND self-terminating, because rising FGF activity represses Grem1. It sets limb SIZE and when outgrowth stops. Nobody has shown that triggering it early removes a limb, and the page says so.

scales.label: Pattern formation
scales.blurb: The reaction-diffusion system that decides how many digits the autopod carries and how they are spaced: a BMP-SOX9-WNT Turing network whose wavelength distal Hox dose sets. This explains autopod FORM. Both published knobs move it toward MORE digits, not fewer, so nothing here has been shown to explain limb absence.

scales.label: Developmental timing
scales.blurb: Apply the lesion when you choose rather than at fertilisation. This is the scale that converts lethal mutants into viable animals and binary genotypes into ordered series, and it is where our recommendation sits. The same Tbx4 deletion gives blocked outgrowth, proximal hypoplasia, or nothing at all, depending only on the hour.

scales.label: Organism / evolutionary comparative
scales.blurb: Four independent natural limb losses - snakes, limb-reduced skinks, cetaceans, stickleback pelvis - solved by at least three different mechanisms at three different layers. They are the ground truth this subject has and ours does not, and they are the reason to present a design space instead of an answer.

scales.label: Non-animal / in vitro
scales.blurb: Budoids, human iPSC limb-bud mesenchyme, limb-bud explants, recombinant limbs and trunk-like structures. The route a modern reviewer asks about first, the route with the best welfare case, and the route whose honest limit is that no dish currently makes a limb.

recommendation.headline: If the goal is a limbless MOUSE EMBRYO with an unambiguous phenotype: conditional Fgf10 deletion restricted to limb-bud mesenchyme (Prx1-CreER) and induced at a chosen stage. If the goal is a VIABLE ADULT ANIMAL: do not attempt tetra-amelia at all - take one pair, with Tbx5-conditional for forelimb or Tbx4-conditional for hindlimb, or take the ZRS-null, which is the only limb-reduced mouse in this literature with a published photograph of it alive and of normal body size at two weeks.
why: It starts from the strongest phenotype in the literature. Fgf10 loss abolishes AER formation and gives complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs; it is the reference amelia and it is upstream of Fgf8.

It removes the thing that makes that phenotype useless. The germline Fgf10 null dies perinatally from complete absence of lungs - a defect with nothing to do with limbs. Prx1-Cre recombines limb-bud mesenchyme from E9.5 and is never detected in limb-bud ectoderm, so the lung, thyroid, pituitary and salivary gland requirements are outside the domain.

It adds the one axis that the whole field has shown to matter. Naiche and Papaioannou removed Tbx4 at three different times and got three different outcomes, one of which was no phenotype at all. A germline allele cannot express that; an inducible one turns the lesion into an ordered series.
Every component is an existing, published reagent. This is a breeding and dosing programme, not an invention.

It gives a scoreable readout. A skeletal preparation either has an autopod or it does not - which is the property that makes this subject a better benchmark than the open-ended design problems our demo is built on.

honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.preferred: Forelimb-only (Tbx5 conditional) or hindlimb-only (Tbx4 conditional). A mouse missing one pair retains the other and is far more likely to thermoregulate, locomote, groom and reach food than a tetra-amelic animal. Tbx5 is the cleaner of the two in principle because the limb FIELD is correctly patterned in its absence - only the bud is never started - and because the germline Tbx4 null dies at E10.5 from chorioallantoic failure, so Tbx4 work is conditional-only by necessity rather than by choice.
honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.already_demonstrated: The ZRS-null is the one allele in this literature where a limb-reduced mouse has been shown alive: Kvon et al. photographed ZRS-/- animals at two weeks with body size comparable to wild type and truncated limbs. But note what it is - TRUNCATION with a retained stylopod and girdle, not amelia. If the ask is 'a mouse with no limbs that lives', nobody in this literature has published one, and the page should not imply otherwise.
honest_alternative_for_a_viable_adult.the_trade_off_stated_plainly: Amelia and viability pull against each other at every layer. Every route that reliably abolishes the limb bud (Fgf10, Fgfr2b, Grem1, WNT3, RSPO2, Meis1/2) takes out lung, kidney or the whole WNT system with it, because the genes that start a limb also start other organs. The only two ways out are tissue restriction (Prx1-Cre) and cis-regulation (ZRS, Pitx1 enhancer) - and cis-regulation, the route evolution actually used twice, delivers truncation rather than absence.

what_we_would_run_ourselves: Score the Kvon 2016 ZRS ortholog series with a genome language model, pre-registering the prediction that it separates human and coelacanth (normal limbs) from cobra (none) and places python between them. The coelacanth case is the sharpest test: it shares LESS sequence identity with human ZRS (57%) than python does (59%) and yet behaves like wild type, so identity alone cannot produce the right answer.

Score the 17 bp E1 indel in both directions on both backgrounds. The published result is asymmetric - reintroducing it into python ZRS restores normal limbs, removing it from mouse ZRS does not alter limb-bud expression. A model that returns a symmetric effect has failed a test whose answer is known in advance.
Record the Ushiki human-to-mouse CTCF discordance as an explicit REFUSAL in our cross-scale coupling layer rather than scoring it.

State the dose law in Lean as a law about a model - a monotone map from an activity variable with a threshold band to a distal-element count - and show Lean rejects mutants with the monotonicity flipped and the threshold moved. That proves our reasoning is consistent. It proves nothing about mice, and we would write both sentences together.
what_we_will_not_claim: We have never scored a limb enhancer. Everything above is proposed, not done.

No registered calibration exists anywhere in our system, so no quantitative bridge from a sequence score to a skeletal phenotype is composable today. The strongest honest output is a RANKING over sequences.
A sequence score is not transcription and transcription is not a skeleton.
We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm. A prediction we cannot test is a hypothesis and we would label it as one.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Severe TRUNCATION of both fore- and hindlimbs with a retained stylopod and girdle; viable to at least two weeks with normal body size. Not amelia.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the single best-studied limb enhancer in vertebrates, and Kvon et al. 2016 is the field's strongest precedent for a REGULATORY change, not a knockout, removing limbs from a mouse. If the judge says 'an enhancer' or 'a regulatory element' rather than 'a gene', this is almost certainly it.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there a proximal stump with no autopod (ZRS) or no limb bud at all (Fgf10/WNT3 class)?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: True tetra-amelia - complete absence of both fore- and hindlimbs, developing to birth, then perinatally lethal from complete absence of lungs. Also absent thyroid, pituitary and salivary glands.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the canonical limbless mouse and has been since 1998. If the judge's animals had NO limb buds and died at birth, this is the mechanism class.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Did the animals breathe? An Fgf10 null has no lungs.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tetra-amelia - complete absence of all four limbs, with craniofacial and urogenital defects - from a homozygous Q83X nonsense allele in a consanguineous family.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It was the first WNT-gene mutation associated with a Mendelian disorder and it is THE classical human 'gene for limblessness'. Note the authors' own caveat: mouse Wnt3 nulls are early-lethal, so this phenotype exists in humans and not in mice.

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: human (allelic series), Xenopus (reciprocal gain), mouse (Lgr4/5/6 triple KO as a negative)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tetra-amelia syndrome with lung aplasia and total absence of the four limbs; severity graded across an allelic series and correlated with impaired RNF43/ZNRF3 binding. The reciprocal deletion of rnf43 and znrf3 in Xenopus triggers SUPERNUMERARY limbs.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: If the judge's claim is recent and human-genetics-based, this is at least as strong a candidate as WNT3 and arguably stronger: an allelic series, measured biochemistry per allele, and a stated master-switch mechanism. It is also the candidate most likely to be missed, because the older literature points at WNT3.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there lung aplasia alongside the amelia, and was there an allelic series rather than a single family?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Mouse: forelimb buds do not form; hindlimbs normal; the limb field itself is correctly patterned. Human haploinsufficiency gives Holt-Oram syndrome - upper-limb and heart defects, NOT limblessness.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the forelimb initiation gene and it directly activates Fgf10. If the judge's phenotype was forelimb-only, this is the first place to look.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Forelimb only? And was there a cardiac phenotype?

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: mouse, stickleback (PITX1 enhancer), human (small patella syndrome for TBX4; Liebenberg syndrome for PITX1)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Tbx4 null: hindlimb field induced and initially patterned, buds fail to develop, embryos die at E10.5 from chorioallantoic failure. Pitx1 null: hindlimb severely impaired but NOT abolished. Pitx1 enhancer deletion in stickleback: viable pelvic loss under positive selection.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: Hindlimb-only phenotype, or work on the stickleback pelvic system. Note Tbx4 does NOT determine hindlimb identity - Pitx1 does.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Hindlimb only? And did the embryos die around E10.5 from the allantois rather than from the limb?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Mouse: 'limbs are absent or truncated' from failure of the AER to differentiate and be maintained, with no stratified skin and absence of all squamous epithelia and their derivatives. Mice are born alive.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the only amelia-class mouse whose lesion is the signalling-centre EPITHELIUM rather than induction or mesenchymal signalling, and it is a prominent human limb-malformation gene. If the judge mentions ectodermal dysplasia alongside the limbs, this is it.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was there a skin, hair, tooth or gland phenotype as well?

judge_gene_candidates.species_of_evidence: mouse (extra toes, Xt), human (Greig cephalopolysyndactyly, Pallister-Hall)
judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: POLYDACTYLY with loss of digit identity, not limb loss. And critically, removing Gli3 from a Shh-null background progressively RESTORES distal limb development.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is one of the most-studied limb genes and the one most often confused with a limb-loss gene by people outside the field. Worth naming so the conversation can rule it out quickly and respectfully.

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Al-Awadi-Raas-Rothschild syndrome - limb/pelvis/uterus hypoplasia-aplasia. A severe human limb-deficiency condition.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is a genuine human 'limb absence' gene and is in the same WNT family as WNT3 and RSPO2's pathway. We read only a record for which PubMed holds no abstract, so we can confirm the syndrome-gene association and nothing about the phenotype's details beyond the syndrome's own name.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was the pelvis and uterus involved as well as the limbs?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Roberts syndrome - craniofacial anomalies and TETRAPHOCOMELIA (severe shortening, not absence, of all four limbs), with loss of sister-chromatid cohesion at heterochromatic regions.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: Tetraphocomelia is often described colloquially as 'limbless'. It is mechanistically a cohesion/cell-division disorder, not a limb-patterning one, which is a useful and non-obvious distinction to be able to draw.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Were the limbs absent, or were they present and severely shortened?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Limb agenesis when both are inactivated in the lateral plate mesoderm; a three-deleted-allele hypomorph gives proximal hypoplasia and loss of POSTERIOR skeletal elements.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: A recent (2021) agenesis result, upstream of Tbx and co-regulating Fgf10 enhancers. If the judge's work is on limb INITIATION rather than outgrowth, this is current.
judge_gene_candidates.distinguishing_question: Was the phenotype dose-dependent across allele number?

judge_gene_candidates.what_it_would_actually_produce: Failure to establish a functional AER and the SHH/FGF loop, with the core limb mesenchyme eliminated by apoptosis; neonatal lethal from absent kidneys plus lung septation defects.
judge_gene_candidates.why_a_researcher_might_say_this: It is the inhibitor arm of the self-terminating loop and a classic limb-bud gene. Also implicated comparatively: a rapidly evolving GREM1 conserved non-coding element in marine mammals.

welfare.framing: A limbless mouse is a severe phenotype. This section is here because a reviewer will expect it and because its absence would be a hole in the page, not as an apology for the science. The relevant question for a licence or IACUC review is not whether the phenotype is severe - it is - but whether the severity is necessary for the question, and whether a less severe route answers it.

severity_classification.point: European severity classification under Directive 2010/63/EU applies to the BREEDING AND MAINTENANCE of genetically altered lines likely to develop a harmful phenotype, not only to experimental procedures. A line that is limbless at birth is authorised as a harmful-phenotype line before any experiment is performed.
severity_classification.evidence_cite: Zintzsch A et al. 2017, Lab Anim 51:573-582, 'Guidelines on severity assessment and classification of genetically altered mouse and rat lines'
severity_classification.evidence_finding: 'Genetic alterations can unpredictably compromise the wellbeing of animals ... the breeding and maintenance of genetically altered (GA) animals which are likely to develop a harmful phenotype has to be authorized.' The Working Group of Berlin Animal Welfare Officers provides a list of symptoms classified as non-harmful, mild, moderate or severe, with monitoring and refinement strategies and specific housing requirements.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Do not let the animal be born. Analyse at E18.5 by skeletal preparation, at E11.5 by reporter assay, at E10.5 by in-situ hybridisation - which is precisely the protocol Kvon et al. used for everything except the two-week viability photograph. The entire ZRS allelic series was characterised on embryos.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: You learn nothing about postnatal viability, locomotion, growth or welfare - which is exactly the question a 'can you make a limbless mouse' claim turns on.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Use a tissue-restricted conditional (Prx1-Cre) so the lesion does not also remove lungs or kidneys. This both improves the science and removes a large, certain source of suffering that is not even the phenotype of interest.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Breeding complexity; a craniofacial domain in the driver that must be checked.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Use an inducible allele so the lesion is applied in the window that matters. A gene removed after its requirement has passed gives no phenotype at all - Naiche and Papaioannou showed this directly for Tbx4 - so stage selection is a way of asking a sharper question with fewer affected animals.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Tamoxifen effects on pregnancy require vehicle controls.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Take one pair rather than four. A forelimb-only or hindlimb-only animal retains locomotion and is a materially less severe phenotype than tetra-amelia, and for most mechanistic questions it answers the same thing.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: None scientifically, for questions about one limb's network.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Replace with ex vivo limb-bud organ culture, where signalling can be manipulated pharmacologically and lineages tracked longitudinally. Tbx4-null hindlimb buds fail to develop in vitro as they do in vivo, so explants reproduce at least some genetic lesions faithfully.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: Animals are still used to source the buds, so this is a refinement and a partial reduction, NOT a replacement, and calling it a replacement would overstate it.

refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.refinement: Replace with budoids - mESC-derived organoids containing AER-like, surface-ectoderm and limb-mesoderm cells, undergoing chondrogenesis-mediated symmetry breaking, at >1,000 budoids per differentiation - or with human iPSC-derived PRRX1+ limb-bud mesenchyme. These are true replacements and they are scalable.
refinements_in_order_of_how_much_they_re.cost: The readouts are cell fate, polarisation and cartilage, not a skeleton and not an animal. No dish currently makes a limb; the Underhill/Arostegui methods chapter said in 2021 that no organoid system effectively modelled limb-development complexity, and budoids (2025) are a real advance on that but not a refutation of it.

what_a_licence_or_iacuc_review_would_tur: Is the severe phenotype necessary for the question, or would a one-pair, conditional, or embryonic-only version answer it? For most mechanistic questions the answer is that it would.
Is a non-animal route available for this specific readout? For cell-fate and signalling questions in 2026, increasingly yes; for skeletal and postnatal questions, no.
What is the humane endpoint and who decides it? A limbless neonate cannot right itself, reach a nipple or thermoregulate normally.
What are the housing requirements? The Berlin guidelines pair severity classification with specific housing and monitoring requirements rather than treating classification as a paperwork exercise.

How many animals does the breeding scheme produce for each informative one? A homozygous conditional on two floxed alleles plus a driver is a demanding cross, and reduction is a breeding-design problem as much as an experimental one.

Precedent exists and is documented: the Kvon et al. transgenic and knock-in work was reviewed and approved by the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory Animal Welfare and Research Committee, mice were monitored daily and inspected weekly by the committee chair, the head of the facility and veterinary staff, and the facility is AAALAC-accredited. Embryonic samples for in-situ and skeletal preparation were dissected blind to genotype, and knock-in and knock-out experiments used a matched-littermate design.
welfare.our_position: We have no animal facility, no IACUC protocol and no wet-lab arm. Nothing on this page was performed by us and no organism, embryo or cell was made by us. The welfare discussion is here because the design space we are describing is one somebody else would have to execute, and a design space presented without its costs is not a design space.

limitations: We ran no experiments. Every route on this page is a reading of someone else's published work, or an explicitly labelled proposal. Nothing here is a result of ours.

ONE source was read at full text (Kvon et al. 2016, via PMC5484524, including figure legends and STAR Methods). Everything else is read at ABSTRACT level, with one exception noted below. No claim on this page is written in the voice of having read a body we did not read.

Summerbell 1974 (PMID 4463222) is cited at LISTING level: the PubMed record resolves and its title and MeSH terms confirm a quantitative AER-excision series in chick, but PubMed holds no abstract for it, so we have read no result statement from that paper and make no quantitative claim from it. The classical premise is restated independently by Lewandoski et al. 2000.

Garavelli et al. 2010 (PMID 21271649, WNT7A / Al-Awadi-Raas-Rothschild) also has no abstract in PubMed. We confirm the syndrome-gene association from the title and MeSH terms and state nothing further about the phenotype.
Every PMID on this page was retrieved from PubMed and resolved to a record during this session; none is quoted from memory or from a secondary summary. DOIs are as returned by PubMed.

SCOPE OF NEGATIVE SEARCHES. All searches were PubMed only, in English, via the pubmed MCP tools. We did not search bioRxiv, medRxiv, patents, theses or non-English sources, and PubMed's query parser ANDs all terms, so a long query returns fewer results than a short one - several of our early searches returned zero for that reason and were repeated with shorter terms. Specific negatives: (1) no molecular mechanism for Lerista limb reduction was found ('Lerista limb reduction skink evolution' returned 4 records, all taxonomic, morphometric or macroevolutionary); (2) no published genetic AER ablation with diphtheria toxin was found ('diphtheria toxin ablation apical ectodermal ridge genetic mouse' returned 4 records, none of them an AER ablation); (3) no auxin-inducible degron study in mouse embryos was found, so the degron route cites dTAG/FKBP work instead; (4) no limb field was found reported in gastruloids or trunk-like structures, searched on PubMed only, which is the wrong place to look first for a 2026 result; (5) no published Prx1-CreER;Fgf10-flox limb series was found, which is why our own recommendation is labelled 'proposed'; (6) no recombinant-limb experiment using mesenchyme from a defined limb-loss genotype was found. Each of these is an absence in OUR search, not an absence in the literature.

Phenotype statements are quoted or closely paraphrased from the abstracts. Where a paper's own authors flag an inference rather than a measurement - Thewissen et al. on HAND2 association, Sun et al. on cetacean ZRS activity, the 41 Ma and 34 Ma dates - we mark it as theirs and do not restate it as a measurement.

The two published human-to-mouse discordances on this page (Ushiki on CTCF/acheiropodia; Niemann on WNT3 viability) are a standing warning that cross-species transfer of a cis-regulatory or viability claim is unsafe, and we did not systematically check every other route for the same risk.

Two founding Fgf10 papers DISAGREE about whether the limb bud initiates: Min et al. 1998 say initiation was abolished, Sekine et al. 1999 say bud formation initiated but outgrowth did not occur. We preserve the disagreement rather than reconciling it.
Route counts are not evidence counts. 'evidence_strength: proposed' appears on four routes and means exactly what it says: nobody has done it. A design space is not a list of results.

We have never scored a limb enhancer, have no registered calibration anywhere in our system, and have performed no functional validation of any sequence-model output we have produced. Any claim about predicting limb phenotype from sequence is a hypothesis and is labelled as one.
